summary: Intermittent evening 5xx surge from streaming fanout + keepalive mismatch causing upstream worker preemptions
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer BlueArc reports elevated 5xx rate (502/503) on streaming routes during evening business hours. Errors began ~2026-03-13 18:05 UTC and show repeated short spikes (1–3 minutes) with increased tail-latency for streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Multiple long-lived streaming client sessions observed disconnecting and failing to resume. Customer reports degraded UX for interactive analytics feature; estimated 12% of streaming calls in the hour experienced errors.

Timeline / Observed pattern:
- 2026-03-13 18:02 UTC: first error cluster; apigw error rate to this tenant increased to 5xx ~18%.
- 18:05–18:12 UTC: short oscillations of 5xx with concurrent rise in upstream preempt events and runtime worker restarts.
- 18:20 UTC: transient decrease, then another cluster at 19:10 UTC with similar pattern.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool serving BlueArc (tenant id: ta-9043) in us-east-1, running model variants redwood/gptx-7b and redwood/gptx-13b-int8.
- Streaming route: /v1/stream/chat (http2). TLS termination at edge, keepalive proxied through streaming-proxy.

Steps to reproduce (customer reproduction):
1) Establish 40 long-lived streaming sessions that send alternating short user messages (~100 tokens) and occasional large prompts (~2500 tokens).
2) Let sessions idle with periodic keepalive pings from the SDK (interval ~25s).
3) Observe intermittent 502/503 responses and session resets after several minutes.

Observed artifacts / logs:
- apigw logs show HTTP/2 RST_STREAM followed by 502 responses from the proxy.
- streaming-proxy metrics show a short surge in concurrent streams per worker followed by worker preempt and SIGTERM -> restart.
- runtime logs: NVML preempt events and 'worker: preempted due to scheduler pressure' entries; no explicit OOMs.
- TLS logs: occasional TLS renegotiation (client-initiated) at time of spikes; keepalive intervals for some clients drifted to 0–2s in traces (SDK bug suspected).

Initial triage notes:
- Pattern suggests amplification: large prompt fanout (long generation) ties up worker threads while many short heartbeats/keepalives increase scheduling overhead at proxy, causing accept/handshake queuing and eventual worker preempt.
- TLS renegotiation coincident with stream spikes appears to increase CPU overhead on proxy and apigw.

Immediate customer-facing message we sent:
- "We're investigating elevated streaming errors impacting some long-lived sessions. Engineering is triaging runtime preemption and proxy scheduling; we'll follow up within the hour with mitigation steps and ETA."
comments: 2026-03-13 18:25 - Support (Aisha): Collected initial logs from BlueArc tenant and escalated to SRE. Noted concurrent keepalive storm patterns in proxy metrics.

2026-03-13 18:40 - SRE (Marco): Attached flamegraph of streaming-proxy CPU during spike; saw frequent context switches and a rising accept queue. Hypothesis: short keepalive intervals from SDK + TLS renegotiation amplifies per-connection CPU.

2026-03-13 19:05 - Eng (Liang Chen): Runtime reports worker preempt events when per-worker concurrent streams exceed ~48. No NVML OOMs, but scheduler marks GPU as busy and signals preempt to reclaim cycles for other tasks.

2026-03-13 19:30 - Support (Aisha): Informed customer of temporary mitigation (client-side keepalive increase) and asked for replication script. Customer provided reproduction harness that generates 40 streams with intermittent large prompts.

2026-03-13 20:10 - SRE (Marco): Deployed a temporary apigw config change to increase accept queue depth for the affected route by 2x and turned on more aggressive connection backpressure in streaming-proxy. Observed reduction in 5xx rate for subsequent spike window.

2026-03-14 09:12 - Eng (Liang Chen): Opening follow-up task to add telemetry: per-tenant streaming concurrency gauge and TLS renegotiation counter to correlate with preempt events. Assigned to runtime team backlog.

2026-03-14 11:00 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed seeing fewer disconnects overnight after applying keepalive workaround and after our temporary edge config change. Asking to keep ticket open while eng implements durable fix.
investigation_notes: Detailed traces show two contributing factors: 1) client SDK bug causing aggressive keepalive behavior (25s configured but observed bursts of 0-2s) leading to high syscall rates at proxy; 2) large prompt fanout holds GPU kernels open for long real-time durations, which reduces worker availability and triggers scheduler preempt signals. Combined, these create a short-lived amplification loop where proxy CPU and runtime scheduler interact and produce 5xx spikes. Correlated metrics: streaming_proxy.cpu_ns, apigw.accept_queue_depth, runtime.worker_preempt_count. No memory OOMs observed. Next steps identified: durable proxy backpressure improvements, runtime scheduler rate-limits per-tenant long-running generation, and customer SDK patch to fix keepalive jitter.
suggested_workaround: 1) Customer: Increase client-side keepalive interval to >=60s and disable client-initiated TLS renegotiation in SDK (patch available in customer SDK v2.3.1). 2) Platform: Applied temporary apigw accept-queue increase and enabled streaming-proxy backpressure—monitoring for regressions. 3) Avoid concurrent large prompt fanout across many long-lived streams until fixes rolled out.
next_steps:
- Engineering to implement per-tenant streaming concurrency telemetry and a soft cap to avoid worker preempt cascade (tracked in runtime backlog).
- Runtime to add a graceful preempt backoff to avoid immediate SIGTERM on scheduler pressure.
- SDK team to publish recommended keepalive defaults and patch to avoid renegotiation.
- Support to coordinate customer validation and keep ticket open until fix rolled out and validated (aim target: 2026-03-20).
